intro: Starting a business brings a long list of things to sort out, and keeping the books in order from day one is one of the most valuable. If you are looking for a startup bookkeeper near you, you likely want someone local who can set things up properly and help you avoid a messy clean-up later. Here is how to find the right person and what to discuss.
need_heading: What people searching for a startup bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: You want a bookkeeper who understands the pressures of a new business and can get your records right from the start.
needs: You need help choosing and setting up bookkeeping software so that categories and processes make sense for your business from the beginning.
You want someone who can explain how to record income and expenses correctly, so you are not faced with a costly clean-up further down the line.
You are preparing to speak to investors or apply for funding and need tidy, reliable records that stand up to scrutiny.
You would like to understand cash runway reporting so you can see how long your current funds will last and plan ahead with confidence.
You want a bookkeeper who is clear about where their work stops and an accountant's begins, especially for year-end accounts and tax advice.
context_heading: What to understand about bookkeeping for startups
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Good set-up saves expensive clean-ups and gives investors confidence in your records. Ask whether a bookkeeper holds professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them, and make sure they are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Mention the type of business you are starting and what stage you are at, for example whether you have begun trading.
Say whether you already use any bookkeeping software or keep records in another way, such as spreadsheets.
Explain what you need help with most, such as setting up software, categorising transactions, or preparing for investor conversations.
Let us know if you have a particular deadline coming up, such as a funding round or your first tax return.
Include your preferred location or area so we can introduce you to a bookkeeper near you.
Mention if you already work with an accountant, so the bookkeeper can fit in with that relationship.
questions_heading: Questions to ask a startup bookkeeper
questions: How would you set up my bookkeeping from scratch so that it stays tidy as the business grows?
Which bookkeeping software do you recommend for a startup like mine, and why?
Can you help me produce cash runway reports so I can see how many months of funding I have left?
How do you make sure my records are investor-ready if I need to raise money?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and by which body?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and where does your work stop and an accountant's begin?

faqs.q: Why is it important to get a bookkeeper at the start of my business?
faqs.a: Setting up software, categories and processes correctly from the beginning makes investment and growth easier later. It also saves you from an expensive clean-up further down the line.

faqs.q: What should I look for in a startup bookkeeper near me?
faqs.a: Look for someone who is supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and ideally holds a recognised qualification such as ICB or AAT membership. Ask about professional indemnity insurance and whether they are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's begins.

faqs.q: How can iComply help me find a startup bookkeeper near me?
faqs.a: We are a free introduction service. You tell us what you need, and we introduce you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who will quote you directly.

faqs.q: What is cash runway reporting and why does it matter for a startup?
faqs.a: Cash runway reporting shows how long your current cash will last at your current spending rate. It helps you plan ahead and make informed decisions about spending and fundraising.

extra_heading: Choosing between a local bookkeeper and an online one
extra: Searching for a startup bookkeeper near me suggests you would value being able to meet in person, perhaps to hand over a shoebox of receipts or to talk through your plans face to face while everything is still new. A local bookkeeper can sit with you as you set up your software and categories, which many new owners find easier than working it out over a screen. That said, plenty of startups work happily with a bookkeeper further away, so it is worth deciding how much the face-to-face contact matters to you before you narrow your search.

When you compare the options you are introduced to, ask each one how they would handle the early set-up: which software they would suggest, how they would categorise your income and spending, and how often you would speak. Ask too how they would report on your cash runway, since a new business needs to know how long its funds will last. Quotes are on application, so ask each bookkeeper to set out what their quote covers and what would fall outside it, then weigh the answers against each other rather than choosing on price alone.

It also helps to be clear about the boundary between bookkeeping and accountancy from the outset. A bookkeeper keeps your day-to-day records in order, while year-end accounts and tax advice usually sit with an accountant, so ask how they would work alongside yours, or whether they can suggest how that side is handled. Check that they are supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or a professional body, and ask about professional indemnity insurance. A short first conversation along these lines will tell you a great deal about how they work.

extra_faqs.q: Should a startup choose a bookkeeper nearby or one they never meet?
extra_faqs.a: It depends on how you like to work. Meeting locally can make the initial set-up of software and categories easier to talk through, while some new businesses are happy to share records and speak by phone or video. Ask each bookkeeper how they would keep in touch and how quickly they would respond.

extra_faqs.q: What is the difference between a startup bookkeeper and an accountant?
extra_faqs.a: A bookkeeper records the day-to-day money coming in and going out and keeps your records tidy, while an accountant typically handles year-end accounts and tax advice. Good bookkeepers are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's begins, so ask about this early.

extra_faqs.q: How do I judge whether a startup bookkeeper's quote is fair?
extra_faqs.a: Quotes are on application, so ask what each one includes, such as software set-up, regular recording and cash runway reporting, and what would be charged separately. Compare the scope as well as the figure, and check that the bookkeeper is supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and holds professional indemnity insurance.
